newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London dragged lower by HSBC.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London dragged lower by HSBC.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London slipped on the back of losses in HSBC Holdings on Friday after weakness in the stock carried over from a heavy fall in Hong Kong.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index fell 11.32 points or 0.07 percent to 15,559.08 by 1355 GMT.

"HongKong Bank was very weak in Hong Kong after Morgan Stanley took the shares off its "buy" list," said one trader. "The stock started strongly here but has now followed through on that weakness and that's what has pulled the index down."
HSBC was trading at HK$262.5 in London compared with a Hong Kong close of HK$265.
"The only other thing we've seen much trade in is Hong Kong Telecom after three covered warrants overnight pushed the shares better," the trader said. "That has followed through in London."
Hong Kong Telecom shares were quoted at HK$20.35 compared with a close of HK$20.15.
Dealers said that despite the Hang Seng's 135 point loss on Friday sentiment remained firm.
"I think we're still in an upward trend," one said. "But nothing goes up in a straight line."
